Alaska Senate candidate Mary Peltola delays campaign stops after car crash
Peltola and her family sustained minor injuries after a driver struck the car transporting group to campaign stop
Mary Peltola , a Democrat who is running for Alaska ’s lone US Senate seat, and her family suffered minor injuries in a car crash while driving to a campaign stop on Saturday, her campaign said.

The family was on its way to the Alaska Federation of Natives annual banquet when another vehicle crashed into the one transporting Peltola and her family, her campaign said in a statement on Sunday. Peltola required medical attention after the collision.

“Mary and her family sustained minor injuries but are in good spirits,” Cheryl Bruce, Peltola’s campaign manager, said in a statement . “Unfortunately, per the advice of medical professionals, Mary’s upcoming events in Fairbanks and Bethel will be rescheduled for later in the week as she takes time to recover.”

Bruce added: “Mary is disappointed that the accident is delaying the start of her Alaska Always tour, and she is eager to get back on the campaign trail to speak directly with Alaskans about her plan to take on the rigged system and lower costs for working families.”

Police responded to a “multi-vehicle collision” at about 6.55pm on Saturday, according to the Anchorage police department. Peltola’s family and the occupant of a second vehicle were taken to a local hospital “with non-life-threatening injuries”, according to the authorities, while the occupant of a third vehicle refused medical transport.
“The circumstances of the collision are under investigation,” reads a statement from the police department.

Peltola, an Alaska Native and former congresswoman, is challenging Republican incumbent senator Dan Sullivan , hoping to become the first Democrat in nearly two decades to represent the state in the Senate. Both candidates have tried to rally support from Alaska Native voters, a key constituency in the high-stakes race that has become one of the most watched in the nation.

On Friday, Donald Trump ordered the justice department to block the certification of the Senate election in Alaska if Sullivan loses. The lawsuit cites potential confusion with another Republican candidate who is listed on the ranked-choice ballot as Daniel J Sullivan Jr , who is a retired schoolteacher.

Peltola’s incident delayed what her campaign announced as the “Alaska Always tour,” an eight-stop push through the last week before election day. Her campaign said she will resume events on Tuesday, with a stop in Homer, Alaska.

阿拉斯加州参议员候选人玛丽·佩尔托拉因车祸推迟竞选活动
一名司机撞上前往竞选站的汽车运输队后，佩尔托拉和她的家人受轻伤
竞选阿拉斯加唯一美国参议院席位的民主党人玛丽·佩尔托拉（Mary Peltola）的竞选团队表示，她和她的家人在周六开车前往竞选站点时遭遇车祸，受了轻伤。
佩尔托拉的竞选团队在周日的一份声明中表示，当时一家人正在前往阿拉斯加原住民联合会年度宴会的途中，另一辆车撞上了载着佩尔托拉及其家人的车辆。碰撞后佩尔托拉需要医疗救助。
佩尔托拉的竞选经理谢丽尔·布鲁斯在一份声明中说：“玛丽和她的家人受了轻伤，但精神状态良好。” “不幸的是，根据医疗专业人士的建议，玛丽即将在费尔班克斯和伯特利举行的活动将被重新安排在本周晚些时候，因为她需要时间来康复。”
布鲁斯补充道：“玛丽对这次事故推迟了她的阿拉斯加永远之旅的开始感到失望，她渴望回到竞选活动中，直接与阿拉斯加人谈论她的计划，即应对被操纵的系统并降低工薪家庭的成本。”
据安克雷奇警察局称，周六下午 6 点 55 分左右，警方对一起“多车相撞”事件做出了反应。当局称，佩尔托拉的家人和第二辆车的乘客被送往当地一家医院，“伤势没有生命危险”，而第三辆车的乘客拒绝接受医疗运送。
警察局的一份声明称：“碰撞情况正在调查中。”
阿拉斯加州原住民、前国会女议员佩尔托拉正在挑战共和党现任参议员丹·沙利文，希望成为近二十年来第一位在参议院代表该州的民主党人。两位候选人都试图争取阿拉斯加原住民选民的支持，阿拉斯加原住民选民是这场高风险竞选的关键选区，已成为全国最受关注的选区之一。
周五，唐纳德·特朗普命令司法部如果沙利文失败，将阻止阿拉斯加州参议院选举的认证。该诉讼指出，与另一位共和党候选人可能存在混淆，该候选人被列为排名选择选票的小丹尼尔·J·沙利文(Daniel J Sullivan Jr)，他是一名退休教师。
佩尔托拉的事件推迟了她的竞选团队宣布的“阿拉斯加永远巡回演出”，该巡回演出在选举日之前的最后一周进行八站巡演。她的竞选团队表示，她将于周二恢复活动，并在阿拉斯加荷马停留。

Blanche says Trump isn't trying to meddle with Alaska election results by suing over Senate race
Attorney General Todd Blanche is defending the Trump administration’s lawsuit to block certification of Alaska's Senate results if incumbent Republican Dan Sullivan loses the race

WASHINGTON -- WASHINGTON (AP) — Attorney General Todd Blanche on Sunday defended the Trump administration's lawsuit to block certification of Alaska's Senate results if Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan loses the race and argued that the legal challenge was a necessary step to avoid confusing voters in the closely watched midterm race .

President Donald Trump , who said Friday that he was "the one that said do it,” is not trying to overturn state election results “in any way, shape or form” on the cusp of the Nov. 3 election, Blanche told CNN's “State of the Union.”
“We wish that we didn’t have to do this. We hope for a resolution that works,” Blanche said.

Republicans fear that a second candidate on the ballot who is named Dan Sullivan — a retired teacher and school administrator from the tiny fishing community of Petersburg — could siphon away votes from the senator and tip the outcome in favor of Democrat Mary Peltola , a former congresswoman.

A day after the lawsuit was filed on Thursday, Peltola called it “just flagrant, flagrant corruption in my opinion” and a diversion tactic by Republicans. Alaska’s other Republican senator, Lisa Murkowski, also criticized the lawsuit in a social media post.
Trump told reporters on Sunday that he believed the ballot was illegal because it was unfair and that Sen. Sullivan should be identified to voters as the sitting senator.
“At least let him use the name Sen. Dan Sullivan as opposed to incumbent, because a lot of people don’t know what incumbent means,” Trump said.
Alaskan voters will see “Dan S. Sullivan” identified as a “registered Republican” and “incumbent” on their ballots, while “Daniel J. Sullivan Jr.” will not have a party affiliation.

Blanche represented Trump as a personal attorney before the Republican president appointed him to lead the Department of Justice, which filed the lawsuit in Alaska. Blanche defended Trump in his election inference case before voters elected Trump to a second White House term, effectively ending the criminal prosecution.

Blanche told CNN host Dana Bash that it was “crazy” for her to ask him if Trump was trying to lay the groundwork for the same sort of election challenges that occurred before a mob of his supporters stormed the U.S. Capitol on Jan. 6, 2021.

“We are not doing anything improper. We’re not doing anything we’re not allowed to do. And we have to let the process play out," Blanche said. "But I do think it’s important for the American people to understand that we are not — (and) President Trump is not — trying to take over a state election in any way shape or form.”
The lawsuit, he told CBS' “Face the Nation,” is meant to “put guardrails in place” to preserve possible evidence of voter confusion at the polls.

“It’s not saying, ‘Don’t certify.’ It’s saying, ‘If a court ultimately determines that it was decided because of confusion and not the will of the voters, then we do not think the states should certify.’ And that’s consistent with federal law and consistent with even Alaskan law, if that happens,” he said.
Associated Press writer Josh Boak contributed to this report.

司法部长托德·布兰奇正在为特朗普政府的诉讼辩护，如果现任共和党人丹·沙利文输掉竞选，该诉讼将阻止阿拉斯加州参议院结果的认证
华盛顿 - 华盛顿（美联社） - 周日，司法部长托德·布兰奇为特朗普政府提起的诉讼进行了辩护，该诉讼旨在阻止共和党现任议员丹·沙利文输掉阿拉斯加州参议院选举结果，并认为法律挑战是避免在备受关注的中期选举中让选民感到困惑的必要步骤。
布兰奇对 ​​CNN 的《国情咨文》节目表示，唐纳德·特朗普总统周五表示，他是“那个说要做就做的人”，他并没有试图在 11 月 3 日大选的风口浪尖上“以任何方式、形式”推翻州选举结果。
“我们希望我们不必这样做。我们希望能有一个有效的解决方案，”布兰奇说。
共和党人担心，选票上的第二位候选人丹·沙利文（Dan Sullivan）是一位来自彼得堡小渔村的退休教师和学校管理人员，他可能会从参议员那里夺走选票，并使选举结果有利于民主党人、前国会女议员玛丽·佩尔托拉（Mary Peltola）。
周四提起诉讼的第二天，佩尔托拉称其“在我看来是公然、公然的腐败”，也是共和党人的转移注意力的策略。阿拉斯加的另一位共和党参议员丽莎·默科斯基也在社交媒体帖子中批评了这起诉讼。
特朗普周日告诉记者，他认为这次投票是非法的，因为它不公平，并且应该向选民表明参议员沙利文是现任参议员。
“至少让他使用参议员丹·沙利文（Dan Sullivan）的名字，而不是现任参议员的名字，因为很多人不知道现任参议员的含义，”特朗普说。
阿拉斯加选民将在选票上看到“丹·S·沙利文”被标识为“注册共和党”和“现任”，而“小丹尼尔·J·沙利文”则被标识为“注册共和党”和“现任”。不会有党派关系。
在共和党总统任命布兰奇领导司法部之前，布兰奇作为特朗普的私人律师代表特朗普，司法部在阿拉斯加提起了诉讼。在选民选举特朗普连任白宫之前，布兰奇在选举推论案中为特朗普辩护，有效结束了刑事起诉。

布兰奇告诉 CNN 主持人达纳·巴什 (Dana Bash)，她问他特朗普是否试图为 2021 年 1 月 6 日他的支持者暴徒冲进美国国会大厦之前发生的同样类型的选举挑战奠定基础，这太“疯狂”了。
“我们没有做任何不当的事情。我们没有做任何不被允许做的事情。我们必须让这个过程顺利进行，”布兰奇说。 “但我确实认为，美国人民必须明白，我们不会——（而且）特朗普总统也不会——试图以任何方式接管州选举。”
他告诉哥伦比亚广播公司的“面对全国”节目，该诉讼旨在“设置护栏”，以保留选民在投票时感到困惑的可能证据。
“这并不是说，‘不要认证’。而是说，‘如果法院最终认定该决定是由于混乱而不是选民的意愿而做出的，那么我们认为各州不应该认证。’这符合联邦法律，如果发生这种情况，甚至也符合阿拉斯加的法律，”他说。

title_en: Blanche defends DOJ lawsuit blocking Alaska Senate results if Republican loses
title_zh: 如果共和党失败，布兰奇将为司法部阻止阿拉斯加州参议院结果的诉讼进行辩护
summary: Attorney General Todd Blanche defended the Justice Department's suit over Alaska's Senate race in an interview on CNN.
summary_zh: 司法部长托德·布兰奇在接受美国有线电视新闻网采访时为司法部就阿拉斯加州参议员竞选提起的诉讼进行了辩护。
body_en: Blanche defends DOJ lawsuit blocking Alaska Senate results if Republican loses

President Donald Trump walks past Attorney General Todd Blanche after speaking at a roundtable event in the East Room of the White House, Wednesday, Oct. 21, 2026, in Washington. Alex Brandon/AP hide caption

U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche Sunday defended his department's lawsuit seeking to stop Alaska from automatically certifying the results of its Senate election if the Republican incumbent there loses.
Earlier this week he had said the Justice Department could get involved in the vote certification process in a "doomsday" scenario.
Week in Politics: Ramaswamy's Ohio ad; Trump greenlights DOJ to sue over Alaska Senate
Pressed on CNN about whether the suit was setting the stage for President Trump to challenge the outcome of next week's midterm elections, Blanche denied it.
The seat is seen as one vital for Republicans if they are to maintain control of the Senate for the second half of President Trump's term in office.

The Justice Department claims that potential confusion over candidates with similar names is the reason for the suit, though some Democrats have argued that it is actually an attempt to interfere in the democratic process.
A candidate on the Nov. 3 ballot is a retired schoolteacher from Petersburg, named Daniel J. Sullivan, with a remarkably similar name to the current Republican senator, Dan Sullivan.

Republicans have accused Daniel J. Sullivan of running as a spoiler to try and divert votes away from the incumbent. But the other Sullivan has said the decision to run was his own and denied his candidacy was intended to confuse voters or siphon votes in Republican Sullivan's tight race against Democrat Mary Peltola, a former congresswoman.

This combination photo shows Sen. Dan Sullivan, R-Alaska, left, in Palmer, Alaska, Aug. 17, 2026, and a candidate in Alaska's Senate race, Dan Sullivan, right, in Petersburg, Alaska, July 3, 2026. Mark Thiessen; Becky Bohrer/AP hide caption
The Justice Department has argued in its suit that the name overlap risks confusing voters.

"We're not laying any groundwork for the president to do that," Blanche told anchor Dana Bash on CNN's State of the Union, after she asked whether the administration was positioning Trump to overturn a result he did not like.
"President Trump is not trying to take over a state election in any way, shape, or form," Blanche added.
The exchange grew heated when Bash raised Blanche's "doomsday" remark to reporters in Virginia.

Bash asked Blanche whether the Alaska case risked repeating some of the events during the aftermath of the 2020 election and the Jan. 6 attacks on the Capitol. "Oh, you got to stop it with that. You are not being a real person. Come on, man," Blanche replied, calling the suggestion "crazy."

The Justice Department's lawsuit has demanded that Alaska not "certify any election results that may be impacted by voter confusion." Blanche insisted the more precise demand for relief from the Justice Department is "to not certify if the law is broken," and that it would ultimately be a question for Alaska and its courts to settle.

Blanche suggested it was "so embarrassing" for CNN that the discussion had turned to Jan. 6, and framed the case as a test of whether Alaska had violated federal law and the Constitution by permitting such a potentially confusing ballot process to continue.
"It is an obligation of the states to avoid confusion, among other things, confusion in the minds of voters in the election process," he said.

A state court and the Alaska Supreme Court kept Daniel J. Sullivan on the ballot, after Republican election officials in Alaska had sought to remove him on the grounds that his candidacy was to mislead voters intentionally. That Alaska court decision, Blanche said, "explicitly didn't consider federal law."

2026 年 10 月 21 日星期三，华盛顿，总统唐纳德·特朗普在白宫东厅举行的圆桌会议上发表讲话后走过司法部长托德·布兰奇。亚历克斯·布兰登/美联社隐藏标题栏
美国司法部长托德·布兰奇周日为其部门的诉讼进行了辩护，该诉讼旨在阻止阿拉斯加州在共和党现任议员失败的情况下自动认证参议院选举结果。
本周早些时候，他曾表示，司法部可能会在“世界末日”的情况下参与投票认证过程。
政治周：拉马斯瓦米的俄亥俄州广告；特朗普批准司法部就阿拉斯加州参议院提起诉讼
当被问及该诉讼是否为特朗普总统挑战下周中期选举结果奠定基础时，布兰奇否认了这一点。
如果共和党想要在特朗普总统任期的后半段保持对参议院的控制，这一席位被视为至关重要。
司法部声称，提起诉讼的原因是对名字相似的候选人可能造成混淆，尽管一些民主党人认为这实际上是试图干涉民主进程。
11 月 3 日投票的候选人是一位来自彼得堡的退休教师，名叫丹尼尔·J·沙利文 (Daniel J. Sullivan)，他的名字与现任共和党参议员丹·沙利文 (Dan Sullivan) 的名字非常相似。
共和党人指责丹尼尔·J·沙利文(Daniel J. Sullivan)参选是搅局者，试图转移现任总统的选票。但另一位沙利文则表示，参选是他自己的决定，并否认他参选的目的是为了迷惑选民，或在共和党人沙利文与民主党人、前国会女议员玛丽·佩尔托拉的激烈竞争中窃取选票。
这张组合照片显示的是 2026 年 8 月 17 日在阿拉斯加州帕尔默的阿拉斯加州共和党参议员丹·沙利文（左）和 2026 年 7 月 3 日在阿拉斯加州彼得堡的阿拉斯加州参议员竞选候选人丹·沙利文（右）。贝基·博勒/美联社隐藏标题栏
司法部在诉讼中辩称，名称重叠可能会让选民感到困惑。
“我们不会为总统这样做奠定任何基础，”布兰奇在美国有线电视新闻网国情咨文节目的主播达纳·巴什询问政府是否让特朗普推翻他不喜欢的结果后说道。
布兰奇补充说：“特朗普总统并不试图以任何方式、形式或形式接管州选举。”
当巴什向弗吉尼亚州的记者提出布兰奇的“世界末日”言论时，双方的争论变得激烈。
巴什询问布兰奇，阿拉斯加案件是否有可能在 2020 年大选和 1 月 6 日国会大厦袭击事件之后重演一些事件。 “哦，你必须停止这样做。你不是一个真正的人。来吧，伙计，”布兰奇回答道，称这个建议“疯狂”。
司法部的诉讼要求阿拉斯加州“不要证明任何可能受到选民混乱影响的选举结果”。布兰奇坚称，司法部对救济的更准确要求是“不证明是否违法”，这最终将由阿拉斯加及其法院解决。
布兰奇表示，对于 CNN 来说，讨论转向 1 月 6 日“太尴尬了”，并将此案视为阿拉斯加允许这种可能令人困惑的投票过程继续进行是否违反联邦法律和宪法的考验。
他说：“各州有义务避免混乱，尤其是选举过程中选民头脑中的混乱。”
州法院和阿拉斯加州最高法院将丹尼尔·J·沙利文保留在选票上，此前阿拉斯加州的共和党选举官员试图将他除名，理由是他的候选资格是故意误导选民。布兰奇说，阿拉斯加法院的裁决“明确没有考虑联邦法律”。

title_en: In Islamophobic Rant, Trump Seeks to Stir Republican Base in Michigan

title_en: Trump rallies for Mike Rogers – and Nicki Minaj’s derriere – in Michigan

body_en: Trump rallies for Mike Rogers – and Nicki Minaj’s derriere – in Michigan
Trump again congratulated Ohio senator’s rear end before his cheeky comment about rapper being ‘hard to miss’
Donald Trump reiterated his apparent love for buxom bums during a rally in Michigan on Sunday where he encouraged the crowd to compliment rapper Nicki Minaj ’s behind.

Trump’s cheeky comments about Minaj’s derriere came as he explained his recent observation on the Republican Ohio senator Jon Husted’s rear end. Earlier in October, Trump said of the former college football player: “I don’t do this with men very often. I started examining his body, because I didn’t know he was a great athlete. And I looked and I watched up and down. I looked at his ass and I looked at the whole – and then I looked at his hands. Look at his hands. He’s got these, like, claws.
“You are a great athlete,” Trump also said to Husted. “Congratulations.”

Trump was speaking at the rally to support Mike Rogers , the Michigan Republican Senate candidate. The Michigan race between Rogers and Democrat Abdul El-Sayed remains neck and neck as both political parties scramble for control of Congress in the upcoming midterm elections . But he couldn’t resist his purported other favorite topic.

This afternoon, Trump said the media buzz about these comments was “fake news” neglecting the athletic context of his statements. Trump said he had just learned Husted was a college athlete when he was “looking at him up and down, and I’m studying him”.

Trump insisted his subsequent crack was “in fun”. “I said: I looked at his ass, and I’ve never done that with a man before. It’s true. Off the record, women yes, men no, OK.”
Trump then shouted out Minaj, who the New York Post said was donned in “head-to-toe Gucci” today. Minaj, the paper also reported, was seen walking with Trump after leaving Air Force One.
“By the way, I looked at one hell of a beautiful ass before – Nicki Minaj ,” Trump said, prompting celebratory woos from the crowd. “That’s hard to miss. That – stand up! That’s hard to miss.
“OK, I’m going to get back to my story, Nicki,” Trump continued following still more cheers. “I hope Nicki wasn’t insulted, but we love Nicki. She’s been with us for a long time.”
Trump made statements about Husted’s tush just over a week ago in Kentucky.

“I examined his ass,” Trump said of Husted, who was not at the event. “And then I looked at his shoulders. I looked at his feet. I looked at his hand. I looked at his jawline. Studied him. He’s got a jawline.
“I then patted him on the shoulder, and it was like a piece of steel. I’m still recovering,” Trump said.
Trump also recently praised the appearance of Ed Gallrein, theRepublican congressional candidate from Kentucky.
Obama rallies rapturous Michigan crowd for El-Sayed: ‘He’ll finish the job we started’

“I needed somebody good, and this guy walks through the door,” Trump remarked of Gallrein, in describing his efforts to find a replacement for anti-Maga incumbent Thomas Massie. “I said, look at this beautiful guy.”
The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment about why Trump has been discussing others’ bodies.
Trump’s comments come amid criticism of his language style, which some have likened to grotesquerie.
body_zh: 特朗普在密歇根州为迈克·罗杰斯和妮琪·米娜的臀部集会
特朗普再次祝贺俄亥俄州参议员的臀部，然后厚颜无耻地评论说唱歌手“很难错过”
唐纳德·特朗普周日在密歇根州的一次集会上重申了他对丰满臀部的热爱，他鼓励人群称赞说唱歌手妮琪·米娜的臀部。
特朗普在解释他最近对俄亥俄州共和党参议员乔恩·赫斯特德臀部的观察时，对米娜的臀部做出了厚颜无耻的评论。十月初，特朗普谈到这位前大学橄榄球运动员时说：“我不经常对男人这样做。我开始检查他的身体，因为我不知道他是一名伟大的运动员。我上下观察。我看着他的屁股，我看着整个 - 然后我看着他的手。看看他的手。他有这些，就像爪子。
“你是一位伟大的运动员，”特朗普还对赫斯特德说。 “恭喜。”
特朗普在支持密歇根州共和党参议员候选人迈克·罗杰斯的集会上发表讲话。罗杰斯和民主党人阿卜杜勒·赛义德在密歇根州的竞选仍然不相上下，因为两个政党都在即将到来的中期选举中争夺国会的控制权。但他无法抗拒他所谓的另一个最喜欢的话题。
今天下午，特朗普表示媒体对这些言论的热议是“假新闻”，忽视了他言论的运动背景。特朗普表示，当他“上下打量他，我正在研究他”时，他刚刚得知赫斯特德是一名大学运动员。
密歇根州居民反对潜在的 64 亿美元数据中心账单：“这太疯狂了”
特朗普坚称他随后的破解是“有趣的”。 “我说：我看着他的屁股，我以前从来没有对男人做过这样的事。这是真的。私下里，女人可以，男人不行，好吧。”
特朗普随后大声喊出米娜，《纽约邮报》称米娜今天“从头到脚都穿着古驰”。该报还报道称，有人看到米娜在离开空军一号后与特朗普一起散步。
“顺便说一句，我以前看过一个非常漂亮的屁股——妮琪·米娜，”特朗普说道，引发了人群的欢呼。 “这很难错过。那个——站起来！那很难错过。
“好吧，我要回到我的故事了，尼基，”特朗普在更多的欢呼声中继续说道。 “我希望尼基没有受到侮辱，但我们爱尼基。她和我们在一起很长时间了。”
特朗普一周前在肯塔基州就赫斯特德的言论发表了声明。
“我检查了他的屁股，”特朗普谈到没有出席活动的赫斯特德时说道。 “然后我看着他的肩膀。我看着他的脚。我看着他的手。我看着他的下巴轮廓。研究他。他有下巴轮廓。
“然后我拍了拍他的肩膀，它就像一块钢铁。我还在康复中，”特朗普说。
特朗普最近还赞扬了来自肯塔基州的共和党国会候选人埃德·加莱因(Ed Gallrein)的亮相。
奥巴马为埃尔赛义德召集密歇根州狂热的人群：“他将完成我们开始的工作”
“我需要一个好人，而这个人走进了大门，”特朗普在描述他为寻找反马加现任托马斯·马西替代者的努力时这样评价加莱因。 “我说，看看这个漂亮的家伙。”
白宫没有立即回应有关特朗普为何一直讨论他人尸体的置评请求。
特朗普发表此番言论之际，他的语言风格受到批评，有些人将其比喻为怪诞。

title_en: Catholic bishops regret White House prayer photo with Trump, say it was used politically
title_zh: 天主教主教对在白宫与特朗普合影表示遗憾，称其被用于政治目的
summary: Two Catholic bishops have expressed regret that they agreed to a White House meeting that produced a publicly distributed photo of them praying with President Donald Trump

body_en: Catholic bishops regret White House prayer photo with Trump, say it was used politically - ABC News
Catholic bishops regret White House prayer photo with Trump, say it was used politically
Two Catholic bishops have expressed regret that they agreed to a White House meeting that produced a publicly distributed photo of them praying with President Donald Trump
Two Catholic bishops have expressed regret about agreeing to a White House meeting that produced a publicly distributed photo of them praying with President Donald Trump.

Milwaukee Archbishop Jeffrey Grob, in a statement titled “A Public Apology,” said Sunday that he had received many questions and comments — some of them distraught — about the meeting on Thursday which he and 11 other bishops attended.
He said the meeting was speedily publicized by the White House with photos and a video, without consent of the participants, and less than two weeks away from the midterm elections .

“I feel a heavy sadness, not only over the pain I caused, but also for the fact that something so sacred to a group of religious leaders, prayer to our Heavenly Father, would be manipulated in that way," Grob said.
The bishop of Des Moines, Iowa, William Joensen, also issued a statement making clear he felt the White House had taken advantage of the bishops.

“I wish I had been more shrewd and less simple, like those who exploited our meeting for partisan political purpose,” he wrote. “I pray I am more prudent and wise going forward, even as I remain resolute in my openness to engaging and praying for political leaders at all levels.”

Asked whether the White House had or hadn't received the bishop's consent for releasing the photos and video, the press office declined to answer that question. Instead, White House spokeswoman Taylor Rogers replied, “There has never been a greater president for Catholic Americans than President Trump, and his strong record proves it."

The White House invitation to the bishops — extended in September — offered discussion about such issues as immigration enforcement, religious worker visas , abortion and use of federal tax credits to support private education, according to Joensen and Grob.

“The meeting was in no way an endorsement of the president, his policies, or his party,” wrote Grob. “We were told the meeting was to be a private discussion, that several Catholic members of the cabinet might make an appearance, and that there could be an opportunity to pray privately with the president.”

Airman killed rappelling from Alamodome's ceiling in Salute to Armed Forces ceremony
“It did not take long thereafter for the White House to post a video and photos of the prayer,” Grob said.

“I soon began receiving messages of serious concern over the possibility that I had inadvertently participated in a political event less than two weeks before a national election,” he added. “I also heard from some who felt wounded because of the ways they or their family had been harmed by the president’s policies.”
“I did not go without reservations. I wish I had heeded them,” Grob concluded. “I apologize for any damage my actions have done."

Collectively, members of the U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops have diverse views on Trump and his administration's policies. Minnesota-based Bishop Robert Barron, for example, agreed to serve on Trump's Religious Liberty Commission, which was filled almost entirely with conservative Christians. Some other bishops vehemently denounced aspects of Trump's tough stance on immigration enforcement , saying it runs counter to Catholic teaching.

天主教主教对在白宫与特朗普合影表示遗憾，称其被用于政治目的
两位天主教主教对同意参加一次白宫会议表示遗憾，该会议公开了他们与唐纳德·特朗普总统一起祈祷的照片
两位天主教主教对同意举行一次白宫会议表示遗憾，该会议公开了他们与唐纳德·特朗普总统一起祈祷的照片。
密尔沃基大主教杰弗里·格罗布周日在一份题为“公开道歉”的声明中表示，他收到了许多关于他和其他 11 名主教参加的周四会议的问题和评论，其中一些令人心烦意乱。
他表示，白宫在未经与会者同意的情况下，迅速用照片和视频公开了这次会议，而且距离中期选举还有不到两周的时间。
格罗布说：“我感到非常悲伤，不仅因为我造成的痛苦，还因为对一群宗教领袖来说如此神圣的事情，即向我们的天父祈祷，会被以这种方式操纵。”
爱荷华州得梅因主教威廉·约恩森也发表声明，明确表示他认为白宫利用了主教们的利益。
他写道：“我希望自己能更精明一些，不要那么简单，就像那些利用我们的会议来达到党派政治目的的人一样。” “我祈祷自己今后能更加谨慎和明智，尽管我仍然坚定地开放地参与各级政治领导人并为他们祈祷。”
当被问及白宫是否已获得主教同意发布这些照片和视频时，新闻办公室拒绝回答这个问题。相反，白宫发言人泰勒·罗杰斯回答说：“对于美国天主教徒来说，从来没有比特朗普总统更伟大的总统，他的出色记录证明了这一点。”
乔恩森和格罗布表示，白宫于九月延长了对主教的邀请，邀请他们就移民执法、宗教工作者签证、堕胎和利用联邦税收抵免支持私立教育等问题进行讨论。
格罗布写道：“这次会议绝不是对总统、他的政策或他的政党的认可。” “我们被告知，这次会议将是一次私人讨论，几位天主教内阁成员可能会出席，并且可能有机会与总统私下祈祷。”

“此后不久，白宫就发布了祈祷的视频和照片，”格罗布说。
他补充说：“我很快就开始收到严重关切的信息，担心我可能在全国大选前不到两周的时间里无意中参与了一场政治活动。” “我还听到一些人因为总统政策对他们或他们的家人造成的伤害而感到受伤。”
“我并不是毫无保留地去的。我希望我当时听从了他们的意见，”格罗布总结道。 “对于我的行为造成的任何损害，我深表歉意。”
总的来说，美国天主教主教会议的成员对特朗普及其政府的政策有不同的看法。例如，明尼苏达州的罗伯特·巴伦主教同意在特朗普的宗教自由委员会任职，该委员会几乎全部都是保守派基督徒。其他一些主教强烈谴责特朗普在移民执法方面的强硬立场，称这与天主教教义背道而驰。

title_en: Iowa’s Senate rivals pitch independence from their parties
title_zh: 爱荷华州参议院竞争对手主张独立于其政党
summary: Ashley Hinson qualified her pledge to be Trump’s strongest ally, while Josh Turek praised the president’s border record.
summary_zh: 阿什利·辛森 (Ashley Hinson) 兑现了自己成为特朗普最强大盟友的承诺，而乔什·图雷克 (Josh Turek) 则赞扬了总统的边境记录。
body_en: Republican Ashley Hinson wants Iowans to know she’ll pick a fight with President Donald Trump. Democrat Josh Turek wants them to know he’ll work with him.

The rivals in Iowa’s closely contested Senate race each sought to establish their independence in separate interviews aired Sunday on ABC’s “This Week,” pitching themselves as willing to put their state ahead of their respective party loyalty.
Asked about her campaign pledge to be Trump’s “strongest ally” in the Senate, Hinson added a condition: “If it’s for Iowa.”

“I will be someone’s ally when they’re with me on the issues that are important to Iowa,” the Republican lawmaker said. “And if they’re wrong, I’m going to pick a fight with them, no matter who that is.”

The conflicting comments come in a state Trump won by 13 points in the 2024 presidential election, but where Democrats now see an opportunity to win their first Senate election since 2008. The president campaigned in Iowa this past week as high fuel costs and frustration with his tariffs complicate Republicans’ efforts to maintain the seat.
Republicans close to Hinson told POLITICO last month that she needed to put some distance between herself and Trump, warning that his tariff agenda and the Iran war were undermining her chances.
On Sunday, Hinson rejected Trump’s positive assessment of the economy. “Well, sure doesn’t feel like it right now,” she said, later criticizing the administration’s dealings with Moscow.

“I don’t think we should be making any deals with Russia,” she said, pointing to her vote for sanctions. Her campaign told POLITICO on Friday that she opposed sanctions relief for Russia while supporting Trump’s use of the Defense Production Act to bolster domestic energy production.

But there were limits to her criticism. While calling for the Iran war to end quickly, Hinson declined to oppose a potential new offensive after the midterms, saying she trusted Trump and the military to determine what needed to be done.
Turek, meanwhile, called himself a “proud moderate” and sidestepped a question about whether Democrats had moved too far left.
“I don’t think a lot about the party as a whole. I think about myself, and I think about Iowa,” the Democratic state representative said.

That pitch follows a primary victory aided by national Democratic support , including from Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer’s leadership PAC — which contributed the maximum to Turek’s campaign, though Schumer did not formally endorse. VoteVets spent more than $10 million advertising on Turek’s behalf. He’s also secured the formal endorsement of former President Barack Obama, who appeared in an ad alongside Turek as the two played basketball.

Asked what Trump had done right, Turek said Trump had done “a better job on the border than Biden, for sure.” He also cited agreement on keeping private equity out of housing and eliminating taxes on tips, overtime and Social Security, while arguing that Trump’s economic policies had concentrated wealth and power.
Also asked whether endorsements mattered, Turek offered a blunt assessment: “Probably not.”
body_zh: 共和党人阿什利·辛森（Ashley Hinson）希望爱荷华州人知道她会与唐纳德·特朗普总统发生争执。民主党人乔什·图雷克希望他们知道他会与他合作。
爱荷华州竞争激烈的参议院竞选中的竞争对手在美国广播公司周日播出的“本周”节目中分别接受采访时，都试图确立自己的独立性，并表示自己愿意将自己的州置于各自政党的忠诚之上。
当被问及她在竞选中承诺成为特朗普在参议院“最强大的盟友”时，辛森补充了一个条件：“如果是为了爱荷华州。”
这位共和党议员说：“当有人在对爱荷华州重要的问题上与我站在一起时，我将成为他们的盟友。” “如果他们错了，我就会和他们打架，不管他们是谁。”
这些相互矛盾的言论出现在特朗普在 2024 年总统选举中以 13 个百分点获胜的州，但民主党现在看到了赢得 2008 年以来首次参议院选举的机会。总统上周在爱荷华州进行竞选活动，因为高昂的燃油成本和对关税的不满使共和党保住席位的努力变得更加复杂。
与辛森关系密切的共和党人上个月告诉《政治》杂志，她需要与特朗普保持一定距离，并警告说，他的关税议程和伊朗战争正在削弱她的机会。
周日，辛森拒绝了特朗普对经济的积极评估。 “嗯，现在肯定不喜欢这样，”她说，后来批评了政府与莫斯科的交往。
“我认为我们不应该与俄罗斯达成任何交易，”她指着自己投票支持制裁说道。她的竞选团队周五告诉《政治》杂志，她反对放松对俄罗斯的制裁，同时支持特朗普利用《国防生产法》来促进国内能源生产。
但她的批评是有限度的。辛森在呼吁迅速结束伊朗战争的同时，拒绝反对中期选举后可能发起的新攻势，并表示她相信特朗普和军方可以决定需要做什么。
与此同时，图雷克称自己是“自豪的温和派”，并回避了民主党是否走得太左的问题。
“我对整个政党的考虑不多。我考虑的是我自己，也考虑的是爱荷华州，”这位民主党州代表说。
这次宣传是在全国民主党的支持下取得初选胜利之后进行的，其中包括参议院少数党领袖查克·舒默领导的政治行动委员会，该组织为图雷克的竞选活动做出了最大贡献，尽管舒默并未正式支持。 VoteVets 为 Turek 花费了超过 1000 万美元的广告费用。他还获得了前总统巴拉克·奥巴马的正式认可，奥巴马在两人打篮球时与图雷克一起出现在广告中。
当被问及特朗普做对了什么时，图雷克表示，特朗普“在边境方面做得比拜登更好”。他还引用了关于阻止私募股权投资住房以及取消小费、加班费和社会保障税的协议，同时认为特朗普的经济政策集中了财富和权力。
当被问及背书是否重要时，图雷克给出了直率的评价：“可能不重要。”

Trump's midterm swing brings him to Michigan as Republicans aim to undermine El-Sayed in Senate race
President Donald Trump's busy midterm campaign schedule is bringing him to Michigan, where Republicans hope to claim an open Senate seat on Election Day
By MIKE CATALINI Associated Press and MIKE HOUSEHOLDER Associated Press

PORT HURON, Mich. -- After weeks of assailing Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed in rallies across the country, President Donald Trump on Sunday is bringing his midterm barnstorming to Michigan, where Republicans see a chance to pick up an open seat on Election Day.
El-Sayed, a former public health official, faces Republican Mike Rogers , a former congressman backed by Trump, in the Nov. 3 race to succeed retiring Democrat Gary Peters.
“We don't want to see a jihadist senator,” Trump told reporters as he left for Michigan. “We don’t want to see a member of the Muslim Brotherhood in our Senate.”

El-Sayed has repeatedly denied unsubstantiated Republican allegations that he is connected to the Muslim Brotherhood , an Islamic movement with branches that the U.S. government has designated as terrorist organizations . The claims by Republicans have been denounced by Democrats as attacks on El-Sayed's faith and his Egyptian heritage. El-Sayed would be the first Muslim senator if elected.

The race has taken on significance beyond Michigan, with Republicans casting El-Sayed as a symbol of a Democratic Party moving further to the left. Progressives, meanwhile, see his candidacy as a test of whether their agenda can win in a battleground state ahead of the 2028 presidential election.

Trump’s visit to Port Huron follows former Democratic President Barack Obama's appearances Saturday in Michigan and Ohio for his party's candidates. It is Trump's latest stop on a packed campaign schedule to bolster Republicans on the midterm ballot as the GOP is weighed down by voters' frustration with the economy and the war with Iran.
Port Huron, about 60 miles (96.56 kilometers) northeast of Detroit, sits across the St. Clair River from Canada, where Trump’s tariffs have strained trade relations between the longtime allies.

Unlike Trump’s earlier trips to Republican-controlled states where his party is on defense, the GOP has not won a Senate race in Michigan for more than three decades. Rogers unsuccessfully ran for Senate in 2024, losing to then-Rep. Elissa Slotkin.
El-Sayed has taunted Trump, encouraging him to come to Michigan in the belief that a visit would backfire on Rogers.
“Donald, if you’re watching, don’t wuss out, man,” El-Sayed said. The progressive, who won a divisive primary in August, has said the country needs to “turn the page on Donald Trump.”
During their second and final general election campaign debate , Rogers questioned El-Sayed's loyalty to the United States.

密歇根州休伦港——在全国各地的集会上攻击民主党参议院候选人阿卜杜勒·赛义德之后，唐纳德·特朗普总统周日将在密歇根州进行中期巡回演讲，共和党人认为那里有机会在选举日获得一个空缺席位。
前公共卫生官员埃尔-赛义德在 11 月 3 日接替退休民主党人加里·彼得斯的竞选中，将与特朗普支持的前国会议员、共和党人迈克·罗杰斯对决。
“我们不想看到一名圣战参议员，”特朗普在前往密歇根州时告诉记者。 “我们不想在我们的参议院看到穆斯林兄弟会的成员。”
埃尔-赛义德一再否认共和党未经证实的指控，即他与穆斯林兄弟会有联系，穆斯林兄弟会是一个伊斯兰运动，其分支被美国政府指定为恐怖组织。共和党人的说法遭到民主党人的谴责，称其为对埃尔赛义德信仰及其埃及血统的攻击。如果当选，赛义德将成为第一位穆斯林参议员。
这场竞选的影响力已经超越了密歇根州，共和党人将埃尔赛义德视为民主党进一步左倾的象征。与此同时，进步派人士将他的候选资格视为对他们的议程能否在 2028 年总统选举前的战场州获胜的考验。
特朗普访问休伦港之前，前民主党总统巴拉克·奥巴马周六在密歇根州和俄亥俄州为该党候选人露面。这是特朗普在紧张的竞选日程中的最新一站，目的是在中期选举中支持共和党，因为选民对经济和与伊朗的战争感到沮丧，这给共和党带来了压力。
休伦港位于底特律东北约 60 英里（96.56 公里）处，与加拿大隔圣克莱尔河相望，特朗普的关税导致这两个长期盟友之间的贸易关系紧张。
与特朗普早些时候访问共和党控制的州不同，共和党在密歇根州的参议员竞选中已经有三十多年没有赢得过胜利了。罗杰斯在 2024 年竞选参议员失败，输给了当时的众议员。艾丽莎·斯洛特金。
埃尔-赛义德嘲笑特朗普，鼓励他前往密歇根州，因为他相信访问会对罗杰斯产生适得其反的效果。
“唐纳德，如果你在看的话，别发脾气，伙计，”埃尔-赛义德说。这位进步人士在八月份赢得了一场存在分歧的初选，他表示，美国需要“翻开唐纳德·特朗普的新一页”。
在第二次也是最后一次大选辩论中，罗杰斯质疑埃尔赛义德对美国的忠诚度。

title_en: Alaska Senate candidate Mary Peltola delays campaign events after car crash
title_zh: 阿拉斯加州参议院候选人玛丽·佩尔托拉因车祸推迟竞选活动
summary: Anchorage police confirmed a crash involving three vehicles occurred Saturday and said those involved sustained “non-life threatening” injuries.
summary_zh: 安克雷奇警方证实周六发生了一起涉及三辆车的车祸，并表示涉案人员“没有生命危险”。
body_en: Mary Peltola delays campaign events after sustaining ‘minor injuries’ in car crash
Former Rep. Mary Peltola is rescheduling several upcoming campaign events after she and her family sustained “minor” injuries in a car crash, her campaign announced Sunday.

“Mary and her family sustained minor injuries but are in good spirits. Unfortunately, per the advice of medical professionals, Mary’s upcoming events in Fairbanks and Bethel will be rescheduled for later in the week as she takes time to recover,” Peltola campaign manager Cheryl Bruce said in a statement.

“Mary is disappointed that the accident is delaying the start of her Alaska Always Tour, and she is eager to get back on the campaign trail to speak directly with Alaskans about her plan to take on the rigged system and lower costs for working families,” Bruce added.

Peltola was en route to the Alaska Federation of Natives’ annual banquet Saturday when a vehicle transporting the candidate and her family was struck by another driver, according to the campaign. A spokesperson for the campaign said they had no reason to believe the accident had been politically motivated.
The police department in Anchorage confirmed Sunday that a collision involving three vehicles occurred on evening and those involved sustained “non-life threatening injuries.”
Police added that the incident is under investigation.

Peltola, a Democrat, is locked in a competitive Senate race against GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan. She was elected to the House in 2022 but narrowly lost her re-election bid in 2024, the same year that President Donald Trump won the state by 13 percentage points .
Sullivan’s re-election race, in which he’s seeking a third term, is tighter than expected, with Alaska voters tying Trump to high gas and grocery prices resulting from the ongoing war with Iran.
Trump and Vice President JD Vance rallied voters in Alaska separately earlier this month.

Republicans have accused Democrats of recruiting another candidate named Dan Sullivan to run for the Senate, saying that voters may be confused by the presence of two Dan Sullivans on the ballot if they plan to vote for the incumbent senator.

Democrats have not taken credit for recruiting the second Dan Sullivan into the race. He’ll appear on the ballot as Dan J. Sullivan, while the incumbent senator will be identified by his name, political party and a clear notation that he’s the incumbent.

Last week, the Justice Department sued Alaska’s election officials, seeking to block certification of the election if Sen. Dan Sullivan loses. It cited Dan J. Sullivan’s presence on the ballot as a point of “ voter confusion .”
On Saturday, Democrats filed a motion urging a federal judge to dismiss the case.
Alexandra Marquez is a politics reporter for NBC News.
body_zh: 玛丽·佩尔托拉在车祸中受“轻伤”后推迟了竞选活动
前众议员玛丽·佩尔托拉（Mary Peltola）的竞选团队周日宣布，她和家人在车祸中受“轻”伤后，她正在重新安排即将举行的几项竞选活动。
佩尔托拉竞选经理谢丽尔·布鲁斯在一份声明中表示：“玛丽和她的家人受了轻伤，但精神状态良好。不幸的是，根据医疗专业人士的建议，玛丽即将在费尔班克斯和伯特利举行的活动将被重新安排在本周晚些时候，因为她需要时间来康复。”
布鲁斯补充道：“玛丽对这次事故推迟了她的阿拉斯加永远之旅的开始感到失望，她渴望回到竞选活动中，直接与阿拉斯加人谈论她的计划，即接受操纵系统并降低工薪家庭的成本。”
据竞选团队称，周六，佩尔托拉在前往阿拉斯加原住民联合会年度宴会的途中，一辆载着候选人及其家人的车辆被另一名司机撞倒。该运动的一名发言人表示，他们没有理由相信这起事故是出于政治动机。
安克雷奇警察局周日证实，晚上发生了三辆车相撞的事故，涉案人员“没有生命危险”。
警方补充说，该事件正在调查中。
民主党人佩尔托拉正在与共和党参议员丹·沙利文展开竞争激烈的参议院竞选。她于 2022 年当选为众议院议员，但在 2024 年连任竞选中以微弱优势落败，同年唐纳德·特朗普总统以 13 个百分点的优势赢得该州。
沙利文寻求第三次连任，他的连任竞选比预期更为激烈，阿拉斯加选民将特朗普与伊朗持续战争导致的高油价和杂货价格联系在一起。
本月早些时候，特朗普和副总统万斯分别在阿拉斯加召集选民。
共和党人指责民主党招募另一位名叫丹·沙利文的候选人竞选参议员，称如果选民打算投票给现任参议员，他们可能会对选票上出现两名丹·沙利文感到困惑。
民主党并没有因为招募第二位丹·沙利文参加竞选而受到赞扬。他将以丹·J·沙利文 (Dan J. Sullivan) 的身份出现在选票上，而现任参议员将通过他的姓名、政党以及明确表明他是现任参议员的身份来识别。
上周，司法部起诉阿拉斯加州的选举官员，寻求在参议员丹·沙利文失败的情况下阻止对选举的认证。它引用丹·J·沙利文在选票上的存在作为“选民困惑”的一个点。
周六，民主党提出一项动议，敦促联邦法官驳回此案。
亚历山德拉·马尔克斯是 NBC 新闻的政治记者。

Blanche says Trump isn't trying to meddle with Alaska election results by suing over Senate race
Politics Updated on Oct 25, 2026 4:00 PM EDT — Published on Oct 25, 2026 2:19 PM EDT

WASHINGTON (AP) — Attorney General Todd Blanche on Sunday defended the Trump administration's lawsuit to block certification of Alaska's Senate results if Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan loses the race and argued that the legal challenge was a necessary step to avoid confusing voters in the closely watched midterm race.

President Donald Trump, who said Friday that he was "the one that said do it," is not trying to overturn state election results "in any way, shape or form" on the cusp of the Nov. 3 election, Blanche told CNN's "State of the Union."
"We wish that we didn't have to do this. We hope for a resolution that works," Blanche said.
WATCH: Trump says he ordered suit to block Alaska Senate results if GOP loses

Republicans fear that a second candidate on the ballot who is named Dan Sullivan — a retired teacher and school administrator from the tiny fishing community of Petersburg — could siphon away votes from the senator and tip the outcome in favor of Democrat Mary Peltola, a former congresswoman.

A day after the lawsuit was filed on Thursday, Peltola called it "just flagrant, flagrant corruption in my opinion" and a diversion tactic by Republicans. Alaska's other Republican senator, Lisa Murkowski, also criticized the lawsuit in a social media post.
Trump told reporters on Sunday that he believed the ballot was illegal because it was unfair and that Sen. Sullivan should be identified to voters as the sitting senator.
"At least let him use the name Sen. Dan Sullivan as opposed to incumbent, because a lot of people don't know what incumbent means," Trump said.
Alaskan voters will see "Dan S. Sullivan" identified as a "registered Republican" and "incumbent" on their ballots, while "Daniel J. Sullivan Jr." will not have a party affiliation.

Blanche represented Trump as a personal attorney before the Republican president appointed him to lead the Department of Justice, which filed the lawsuit in Alaska. Blanche defended Trump in his election inference case before voters elected Trump to a second White House term, effectively ending the criminal prosecution.
WATCH: What's going on with Dan Sullivan and Dan Sullivan? The Alaska Senate litigation, explained

Blanche told CNN host Dana Bash that it was "crazy" for her to ask him if Trump was trying to lay the groundwork for the same sort of election challenges that occurred before a mob of his supporters stormed the U.S. Capitol on Jan. 6, 2021.

"We are not doing anything improper. We're not doing anything we're not allowed to do. And we have to let the process play out," Blanche said. "But I do think it's important for the American people to understand that we are not — (and) President Trump is not — trying to take over a state election in any way shape or form."
The lawsuit, he told CBS' "Face the Nation," is meant to "put guardrails in place" to preserve possible evidence of voter confusion at the polls.

"It's not saying, 'Don't certify.' It's saying, 'If a court ultimately determines that it was decided because of confusion and not the will of the voters, then we do not think the states should certify.' And that's consistent with federal law and consistent with even Alaskan law, if that happens," he said.

华盛顿（美联社）——周日，司法部长托德·布兰奇为特朗普政府提起的诉讼进行了辩护，该诉讼旨在阻止共和党现任议员丹·沙利文输掉阿拉斯加州参议院选举结果，并认为法律挑战是避免在备受关注的中期选举中让选民感到困惑的必要步骤。
布兰奇对 ​​CNN 的《国情咨文》节目表示，唐纳德·特朗普总统周五表示，他是“那个说做就做的人”，他并没有试图在 11 月 3 日大选的风口浪尖上“以任何方式、形式”推翻州选举结果。
“我们希望我们不必这样做。我们希望能有一个有效的解决方案，”布兰奇说。
观看：特朗普表示，如果共和党失败，他将下令提起诉讼，阻止阿拉斯加州参议院的结果
共和党人担心，选票上的第二位候选人丹·沙利文（Dan Sullivan）是一位来自彼得堡小渔村的退休教师和学校管理人员，他可能会从参议员那里夺走选票，并使选举结果有利于前国会女议员、民主党人玛丽·佩尔托拉（Mary Peltola）。
周四提起诉讼的第二天，佩尔托拉称其“在我看来是公然、公然的腐败”，是共和党人的转移注意力的策略。阿拉斯加的另一位共和党参议员丽莎·默科斯基也在社交媒体帖子中批评了这起诉讼。
特朗普周日告诉记者，他认为这次投票是非法的，因为它不公平，并且应该向选民表明参议员沙利文是现任参议员。
“至少让他使用参议员丹·沙利文的名字，而不是现任参议员的名字，因为很多人不知道现任参议员的含义，”特朗普说。
阿拉斯加选民将在选票上看到“丹·S·沙利文”被标识为“注册共和党”和“现任”，而“小丹尼尔·J·沙利文”则被标识为“注册共和党”和“现任”。不会有党派关系。
在共和党总统任命布兰奇领导司法部之前，布兰奇作为特朗普的私人律师代表特朗普，司法部在阿拉斯加提起了诉讼。在选民选举特朗普连任白宫之前，布兰奇在选举推论案中为特朗普辩护，有效结束了刑事起诉。

布兰奇告诉 CNN 主持人达纳·巴什 (Dana Bash)，她问他特朗普是否试图为 2021 年 1 月 6 日他的支持者暴徒冲进美国国会大厦之前发生的同样类型的选举挑战奠定基础，这太“疯狂”了。
“我们没有做任何不当的事情。我们没有做任何不被允许做的事情。我们必须让这个过程顺利进行，”布兰奇说。 “但我确实认为，美国人民必须明白，我们不会——（而且）特朗普总统也不会——试图以任何方式接管州选举。”
他告诉哥伦比亚广播公司的“面对全国”节目，该诉讼旨在“设置护栏”，以保留选民在投票时感到困惑的可能证据。
“这并不是说‘不要认证’。”它的意思是，“如果法院最终认定该决定是由于混乱而不是选民的意愿而做出的，那么我们认为各州不应该证明这一点。”这符合联邦法律，如果发生这种情况，甚至也符合阿拉斯加法律，”他说。

title_en: Peltola postpones campaign stops after Saturday car crash
title_zh: 佩尔托拉在周六车祸后推迟了竞选活动
summary: The Alaska Senate candidate and her family sustained minor injuries, her campaign announced Sunday.
summary_zh: 阿拉斯加州参议员候选人及其家人受轻伤，她的竞选团队周日宣布。
body_en: Former Rep. Mary Peltola is postponing campaign stops in her bid for Alaska’s Senate seat after she and her family sustained minor injuries in a car crash Saturday night.
Peltola and her family were traveling to the Alaska Federation of Natives’ annual banquet when another driver struck their vehicle, her campaign announced Sunday on social media.

“Mary and her family sustained minor injuries but are in good spirits,” campaign manager Cheryl Bruce said in the statement. “Unfortunately, per the advice of medical professionals, Mary’s upcoming events in Fairbanks and Bethel will be rescheduled for later in the week as she takes time to recover.”

Anchorage police said a vehicle rear-ended the car carrying Peltola at a red light Saturday evening, pushing it into a third vehicle. Peltola and the other passengers of her car were taken to a local hospital with non-life-threatening injuries, police said.
The driver who struck their vehicle was also hospitalized with non-life-threatening injuries. Police said the crash remains under investigation.

The crash disrupts the start of Peltola’s eight-community “Alaska Always Tour,” a seven-day campaign swing ahead of the midterms. Events in Fairbanks and Bethel originally scheduled for Sunday and Monday will be rescheduled, while stops in Homer, Kenai, Seward, Juneau, Anchorage and Palmer will continue as planned, the campaign said.
The midterm elections are just over a week away.
Peltola, a Democrat, is challenging Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan in a closely watched race that could help determine control of the Senate.

The race on Thursday became the subject of a Justice Department lawsuit seeking to block certification of the election results if Sullivan loses in November. The administration is arguing that the presence of an independent candidate also named Dan Sullivan is an effort to mislead voters, despite the Alaska Supreme Court allowing the other Sullivan to remain on the ballot in a June ruling.

Attorney General Todd Blanche defended the lawsuit Sunday, arguing that voters could confuse the two candidates. Peltola’s campaign called the suit a “despicable political threat to overturn the election.” Republican Sen. Lisa Murkowski (R-Alaska) piled on, saying the Justice Department's suit should never have been filed.

Alaska’s political history has been marked by fatal transportation disasters. Peltola’s husband, Eugene “Buzzy” Peltola Jr., died in September 2023 when the small plane he was piloting crashed after takeoff in southwestern Alaska. Former Republican Sen. Ted Stevens died in a plane crash in 2010 near Dillingham, and Democratic Rep. Nick Begich disappeared in 1972 after disembarking from Anchorage on a small plane traveling to Juneau.
body_zh: 前众议员玛丽·佩尔托拉（Mary Peltola）和她的家人在周六晚上的一场车祸中受了轻伤，她正在推迟竞选阿拉斯加州参议员席位的竞选活动。
佩尔托拉的竞选团队周日在社交媒体上宣布，当时佩尔托拉和她的家人正在前往阿拉斯加原住民联合会的年度宴会，另一名司机撞上了他们的车辆。
竞选经理谢丽尔·布鲁斯在声明中表示：“玛丽和她的家人受了轻伤，但精神状态良好。” “不幸的是，根据医疗专业人士的建议，玛丽即将在费尔班克斯和伯特利举行的活动将被重新安排在本周晚些时候，因为她需要时间来康复。”
安克雷奇警方表示，周六晚上红灯时，一辆汽车追尾了载有佩尔托拉的汽车，将其撞向第三辆车。警方称，佩尔托拉和车上的其他乘客被送往当地一家医院，伤势没有生命危险。
撞上车辆的司机也被送往医院，没有生命危险。警方表示，事故仍在调查中。
这次事故扰乱了佩尔托拉八个社区的“阿拉斯加永远之旅”的开始，这是中期选举前为期 7 天的竞选活动。该活动表示，原定于周日和周一在费尔班克斯和伯特利举行的活动将重新安排，而在荷马、基奈、苏厄德、朱诺、安克雷奇和帕尔默的活动将按计划继续进行。
距离中期选举只剩一周多了。
民主党人佩尔托拉正在一场备受关注的竞选中挑战共和党参议员丹·沙利文，这场竞选可能有助于确定参议院​​的控制权。
周四的竞选成为司法部诉讼的主题，如果沙利文在 11 月失败，司法部将阻止对选举结果的认证。政府认为，尽管阿拉斯加最高法院在六月的裁决中允许另一位沙利文继续留在选票上，但一位也叫丹·沙利文的独立候选人的出现是在误导选民。
司法部长托德·布兰奇周日为这起诉讼进行了辩护，称选民可能会混淆两位候选人。佩尔托拉的竞选团队称该诉讼是“推翻选举的卑鄙政治威胁”。共和党参议员丽莎·穆尔科斯基（阿拉斯加州共和党人）继续说道，司法部根本不应该提起诉讼。

阿拉斯加的政治历史以致命的交通灾难为标志。佩尔托拉的丈夫小尤金·“巴兹”·佩尔托拉于 2023 年 9 月去世，当时他驾驶的小型飞机在阿拉斯加西南部起飞后坠毁。前共和党参议员特德·史蒂文斯 (Ted Stevens) 于 2010 年在迪林厄姆 (Dillingham) 附近的一次飞机失事中丧生，民主党众议员尼克·贝吉奇 (Nick Begich) 于 1972 年乘坐一架飞往朱诺的小型飞机从安克雷奇下飞机后失踪。

body_en: Blanche defends DoJ’s pre-emptive suit to block Alaska Senate results certification | US midterm elections 2026
Blanche defends DoJ’s pre-emptive suit to block Alaska Senate results certification
US attorney general calls CNN ‘crazy’ for suggesting Trump’s attempt to overturn election could lead to January 6 repeat

Todd Blanche , Donald Trump ’s attorney general, lashed out during an interview on Sunday while defending the justice department’s pre-emptive lawsuit to block certification of Alaska ’s US Senate results if the GOP incumbent loses, calling a TV host’s question “crazy”.

The testy repartee unfolded on CNN’s State of the Union over the DoJ’s unprecedented legal action, which alleges that there could be “voter confusion” due to two candidates named Dan Sullivan on Alaska’s ballot. Trump told reporters , “I’m the one that said do it” when asked about the suit.
Trump says he ordered DoJ to file lawsuit to block Alaska Senate results certification
Dana Bash, State of the Union host, said “one of the big questions is whether or not “Trump tries to overturn the election, and the result of that could be, God forbid, what we saw after January 6”.
“Oh, stop it,” Blanche said. “Oh, you got to stop it with that. You are not being a real person. Come on, man.

“I would have said that before January 6,” Bash said, referring to election-denying Trump supporters’ shocking attack on the Capitol . A bipartisan Senate report said there were seven deaths in relation to this incident.

“Because the president, because the Department of Justice, is concerned that there is an absolute fraud happening in Alaska , and he wants to do something about it, you’re saying, Mr Attorney General, because the president of the United States wants to stop a fraud and confusion in Alaska, is he going to do something crazy? That is not, that is not a real question.”
“We’re not laying any groundwork for the president to do that,” a fiery Blanche insisted. “What I said is the groundwork that we are laying is for Alaska, for the state of Alaska.”
“If it becomes an issue after the election, we’ll have the ability to determine whether there was confusion that violates the law in determining who the senators should be.”
Blanche also appeared irked during an interview with Margaret Brennan on CBS’s Face the Nation after she summed up the litigation and asked whether Trump directed him to file suit.
“Well first of all, let me correct you, OK,” Blanche said. “You described facts that were just simply either at best misleading, but really a lie to your viewers.”
Alaska’s Mary Peltola is making Republicans nervous with Senate control at stake

While Trump’s DoJ has claimed there might be “voter confusion” on Alaskan ballots, potentially propelling Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola to victory, election experts maintain that this position is legally weak.
“The legal claim is so absurdly thin, there’s essentially no likelihood of success,” said Derek Mueller, a law professor at the University of Notre Dame, in a blogpost .

Another expert, David Becker, executive director of the Center for Election Innovation & Research, said this suit marked “an unprecedented intervention by the federal government” and noted that Alaska’s courts had “fully litigated” this issue.

The lawsuit , Becker said, “raises serious concerns about political interference” and that he could not remember “ever attempting to stop the certification of an election – and certainly not 11 days before polls close”.
Richard H Pildes, a law professor at New York University who focuses on elections, told the New York Times: “It is one of the weakest election lawsuits I’ve ever seen.”

美国司法部长称 CNN“疯狂”，称其暗示特朗普试图推翻选举可能导致 1 月 6 日重演
唐纳德·特朗普(Donald Trump)的司法部长托德·布兰奇(Todd Blanche)周日在接受采访时猛烈抨击，同时为司法部的先发制人诉讼进行辩护，如果共和党现任议员输了，司法部将阻止对阿拉斯加美国参议院结果的认证，称电视主持人的问题“疯狂”。
美国有线电视新闻网 (CNN) 的国情咨文节目对美国司法部前所未有的法律行动展开了激烈的对答，该行动声称阿拉斯加选票上两名名为丹·沙利文的候选人可能会造成“选民混乱”。当被问及这套诉讼时，特朗普告诉记者，“我是那个说这样做的人”。
特朗普表示，他命令司法部提起诉讼，阻止阿拉斯加州参议院结果认证
《国情咨文》主持人达纳·巴什 (Dana Bash) 表示，“其中一个大问题是，‘特朗普是否试图推翻选举，上帝保佑，其结果可能是我们 1 月 6 日之后看到的情况’”。
“哦，别说了，”布兰奇说。 “哦，你必须停止这样的行为。你不是一个真正的人。来吧，伙计。
“我会在 1 月 6 日之前这么说，”巴什说，他指的是否认选举的特朗普支持者对国会大厦的令人震惊的袭击。参议院两党报告称，此次事件造成七人死亡。
“因为总统，因为司法部，担心阿拉斯加发生了绝对的欺诈行为，他想对此采取行动，司法部长先生，你说，因为美国总统想要阻止阿拉斯加的欺诈和混乱，他会做一些疯狂的事情吗？那不是，这不是一个真正的问题。”
“我们不会为总统这样做奠定任何基础，”脾气暴躁的布兰奇坚持说。 “我所说的是，我们正在为阿拉斯加、为阿拉斯加州奠定基础。”
“如果选举后这成为一个问题，我们将有能力确定在确定参议员应该是谁时是否存在违反法律的混乱。”
布兰奇在接受哥伦比亚广播公司“面向全国”节目的玛格丽特·布伦南采访时，在总结诉讼并询问特朗普是否指示他提起诉讼后，也显得很恼火。
“首先，让我纠正你，好吧，”布兰奇说。 “你描述的事实充其量只是误导，但实际上是对观众的谎言。”
阿拉斯加州的玛丽·佩尔托拉（Mary Peltola）因参议院控制权受到威胁而让共和党人感到紧张
尽管特朗普的司法部声称阿拉斯加选票可能存在“选民混乱”，这可能会推动民主党参议院候选人玛丽·佩尔托拉获胜，但选举专家坚持认为，这一立场在法律上是薄弱的。
圣母大学法学教授德里克·穆勒 (Derek Mueller) 在一篇博文中表示：“法律主张的力度如此薄弱，几乎没有成功的可能性。”
另一位专家、选举创新与研究中心执行主任戴维·贝克尔表示，这起诉讼标志着“联邦政府前所未有的干预”，并指出阿拉斯加法院已“全面提起诉讼”这一问题。
贝克尔表示，这起诉讼“引发了人们对政治干预的严重担忧”，而且他不记得“曾经试图阻止选举认证——尤其是在投票结束前 11 天”。
纽约大学专注于选举的法学教授理查德·H·皮尔德斯 (Richard H Pildes) 告诉《纽约时报》：“这是我见过的最弱的选举诉讼之一。”

Week in Politics: Ramaswamy’s Ohio ad; Trump greenlights DOJ to sue over Alaska Senate Ohio GOP gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy refuses to withdrawal an explosive attack ad, and President Trump greenlights the DOJ to file a lawsuit about Alaska's senate race.
Week in Politics: Ramaswamy's Ohio ad; Trump greenlights DOJ to sue over Alaska Senate
Ohio GOP gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy refuses to withdrawal an explosive attack ad, and President Trump greenlights the DOJ to file a lawsuit about Alaska's senate race.

Midterm politics grew especially ugly this week in Ohio. The Republican candidate for governor, Vivek Ramaswamy, released an attack ad against his Democratic opponent, Amy Acton. The ad featured Acton's estranged mother who called her daughter a liar and urged Ohioans not to vote for her. But a lot of context - much of it sad and upsetting - was missing from that ad. And before we go on, please be aware we're about to talk about allegations of sexual abuse. NPR senior political contributor Ron Elving joins us. Ron, thanks for being with us.
RON ELVING, BYLINE: Good to be with you, Scott.

SIMON: Legal documents from nearly 50 years ago show that Amy Acton, then 12, and her younger brother were removed from their mother's home following their stepfather's arrest. He was charged with sexual conduct with a minor, fled the state with their mother. He died without facing trial. Amy Acton says he raped her and that she had been sexually abused beginning when she was just 9 years old. The ad has been condemned, including by the current Republican governor, and yet, Ramaswamy continues to defend it. Why?

ELVING: There's an old expression I think we all know - in for a dime in for a dollar. If you're going to risk your statewide campaign and the tens of millions of dollars that Elon Musk and others have invested in it, if you are already risking all that on this kind of tactics - this ad that's divided the Republican Party in Ohio and nationally - then it's not surprising that you choose to defend it. The same goes for Ramaswamy backers, like Vice President JD Vance, who condemned, but rather Republicans who criticized it, calling them whiners - or, for that matter, President Trump, who could have easily stayed out of it but waded in with both feet, telling Ramaswamy to keep the ad running.
SIMON: Is this something with a potential damage to not just Ramaswamy, but other Republicans this election?

ELVING: It might well be in Ohio, where this has dominated conversation, it could blow back on the party's embattled Senate incumbent, Jon Husted, who's in a tight race for reelection against Democratic former Senator Sherrod Brown. Beyond that, any campaigning of this sort, any controversy like this, it just tends to be dispiriting and may discourage people who don't just automatically turn out for midterms.

SIMON: Yesterday, with less than two weeks to go in this election, the Department of Justice filed a lawsuit with a special request of a federal judge about the U.S. Senate race in Alaska. Please tell us about this.

ELVING: Yes. The state of Alaska has a ranked-choice system where the primary election sends several top finishers on to November regardless of party. So the incumbent Senator Dan Sullivan is on the ballot as a Republican, and there's another Dan Sullivan - different middle initial - who also got enough primary votes for the fall ballot. Now, he's not the official Republican Party candidate, even though he's a registered Republican. That's legal in Alaska, but it angered the president, so he sent in the Justice Department to sue to block the certification of results in this election if Trump's preferred Dan Sullivan doesn't win.

We saw Trump in his first term getting angry with people in his Justice Department who pushed back on some of his orders, who chose to follow the law and previous policy instead. Trump has since tried to get rid of those people and replace them with lawyers who will do what he wants. So there are many who fear what might be next if Trump isn't pleased with the election results around the country 10 days from now.
SIMON: Ron, I understand the Brewers were going to call you in to pinch hit last night but won despite that. What's it feel like in Milwaukee?
ELVING: (Laughter) Oh, my goodness. You and I both grew up in Chicago, Scott. We're Cub fans for life, but it turns out that grandsons have a way of scrambling even one's baseball loyalties.
SIMON: Well, NPR's Ron Elving. Thanks so much for being with us.

政治周：拉马斯瓦米的俄亥俄州广告；特朗普批准司法部就阿拉斯加参议院俄亥俄州共和党州长候选人维韦克·拉马斯瓦米拒绝撤回爆炸性攻击广告提起诉讼，特朗普总统批准司法部就阿拉斯加州参议员竞选提起诉讼。
政治周：拉马斯瓦米的俄亥俄州广告；特朗普批准司法部就阿拉斯加州参议院提起诉讼
俄亥俄州共和党州长候选人维韦克·拉马斯瓦米拒绝撤回爆炸性攻击广告，特朗普总统批准司法部就阿拉斯加州参议员竞选提起诉讼。
本周俄亥俄州的中期选举政治变得尤其丑陋。共和党州长候选人维韦克·拉马斯瓦米发布了一则攻击民主党对手艾米·阿克顿的广告。该广告以阿克顿关系疏远的母亲为主角，她称她的女儿是骗子，并敦促俄亥俄州人不要投票给她。但该广告缺少很多背景信息——其中大部分是悲伤和不安的。在我们继续之前，请注意我们将讨论性虐待指控。 NPR 高级政治撰稿人 Ron Elving 加入我们。罗恩，谢谢你和我们在一起。
罗恩·埃尔文连线：很高兴和你在一起，斯科特。
西蒙：近 50 年前的法律文件显示，继父被捕后，当时 12 岁的艾米·阿克顿 (Amy Acton) 和她的弟弟被从母亲的家中带走。他被指控与未成年人发生性行为，并与母亲逃离该州。他未经审判就去世了。艾米·阿克顿 (Amy Acton) 称，他强奸了她，而她从 9 岁时就开始遭受性虐待。该广告遭到包括现任共和党州长在内的谴责，但拉马斯瓦米继续为其辩护。为什么？

ELVING：我想我们都知道一个古老的表达方式——一分钱一分货。如果你要拿全州竞选活动以及埃隆·马斯克和其他人投入的数千万美元冒险，如果你已经在这种策略上冒着所有风险——这则广告在俄亥俄州和全国范围内分裂了共和党——那么你选择捍卫它就不足为奇了。拉马斯瓦米的支持者也是如此，比如副总统万斯（JD Vance）谴责了这一做法，而共和党人则批评了拉马斯瓦米，称他们为牢骚者——或者就这一点而言，特朗普总统本可以轻易置身事外，但却双脚介入，告诉拉马斯瓦米继续投放广告。
西蒙：这是否不仅会对拉马斯瓦米造成潜在损害，还会对本次选举的其他共和党人造成潜在损害？
埃尔文：很可能在俄亥俄州，这件事在当地占据主导地位，这可能会对该党陷入困境的现任参议院议员乔恩·赫斯特德(Jon Husted)造成回击，他正在与民主党前参议员谢罗德·布朗(Sherrod Brown)争夺连任。除此之外，任何此类竞选活动、任何此类争议，都往往会令人沮丧，并可能使那些不自动参加中期选举的人灰心丧气。
西蒙：昨天，距离本次选举还有不到两周的时间，司法部就阿拉斯加的美国参议院竞选向联邦法官提起了一项特别请求。请告诉我们这件事。

埃尔文：是的。阿拉斯加州有一个排名选择制度，初选将几名排名前列的人选入 11 月，无论党派如何。因此，现任参议员丹·沙利文作为共和党人参加了选票，还有另一位丹·沙利文——中间名首字母不同——也为秋季投票获得了足够的初选票。现在，他不是正式的共和党候选人，尽管他是注册的共和党人。这在阿拉斯加是合法的，但这激怒了总统，因此如果特朗普喜欢的丹·沙利文没有获胜，他派司法部提起诉讼，阻止对这次选举结果的认证。
我们看到特朗普在他的第一个任期内对司法部的人感到愤怒，这些人拒绝了他的一些命令，而是选择遵守法律和之前的政策。此后，特朗普试图摆脱这些人，并用愿意做他想做的事情的律师取而代之。因此，很多人担心，如果特朗普对 10 天后全国各地的选举结果不满意，接下来会发生什么。
西蒙：罗恩，我知道酿酒人队昨晚打算叫你来代打，但尽管如此还是赢了。在 密尔沃基 是什么感觉？
埃尔文：（笑声）哦，天哪。你和我都在芝加哥长大，斯科特。我们一生都是小熊队的球迷，但事实证明，孙子们甚至有办法扰乱一个人对棒球的忠诚度。
西蒙：嗯，是 NPR 的罗恩·埃尔文。非常感谢您与我们在一起。

title_en: Israel to close West Bank crossings before elections amid military operation
title_zh: 以色列将在军事行动期间在选举前关闭西岸过境点
summary: The Israeli military's operation comes in response to a gun attack that killed two Israeli soldiers and wounded three others in the West Bank.
summary_zh: 以色列军方采取行动是为了回应西岸发生的枪击事件，该事件造成两名以色列士兵死亡、三人受伤。
body_en: Israeli military to close West Bank crossings ahead of upcoming elections as massive operation underway - CBS News
The Israeli military continued a massive operation in the occupied West Bank on Sunday, placing major restrictions on movement ahead of Israel's upcoming elections.
The operation, which comes in response to a gun attack that killed two Israeli soldiers and wounded three others in Hebron on Friday, has displaced hundreds of Palestinians over the last two days.

In Hebron, more than 2,200 people, including nearly 200 children under the age of 18, have been displaced, the municipality said. Since Friday's attack, all entrances and exits to the city have remained sealed, with the epicenter of the operation in Deir Bahha and another part of the city called Al-Jalda, according to Hebron Mayor Yousef Zuhair Al-Jabari.
"People cannot reach or enter the city, and they cannot leave it. The blockade has affected every aspect of life," Al-Jabari said.
The Israeli military said it operated in more than 400 different locations over the weekend and arrested 40 Palestinians it claimed were affiliated with Hamas or Palestinian Islamic Jihad.

Additionally, the Israeli military said most Palestinian workers with permits will not be allowed to enter Israeli settlements for work on Sunday and Monday, and crossings into Israel will remain closed until after Tuesday's Israeli elections.
The election is largely seen as a referendum on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu 's leadership and security policies during the past three years of war.

Six Israelis have been killed this year in attacks in the West Bank, which is experiencing a surge of violence . During the same period, 112 Palestinians have been killed, according to the Ramallah-based Palestinian Health Ministry.

Friday's attack sparked outrage in Israel, with Netanyahu and three members of his right-wing government giving statements from the site of the attack on Friday afternoon, vowing to respond forcefully .
"We warned a few weeks ago about attempts by our enemies to harm us, our citizens and our soldiers ahead of the election," Netanyahu said. "We will act to destroy this place."

Netanyahu, who is running for reelection in next week's elections and has received President Trump's endorsement , is under pressure to demonstrate a strong show of force against Palestinian attackers to bolster his image for Israelis concerned with security.

Roughly 3 million Palestinians and 540,000 Israeli settlers live in the West Bank, which Israel occupied in the 1967 Mideast war. Hebron is one of its most tense cities and the only place where Jewish settlers live in the heart of a densely populated Palestinian area under Israeli military protection.

body_zh: 以色列军方将在即将举行的选举前关闭西岸过境点，大规模行动正在进行中 - 哥伦比亚广播公司新闻
周日，以色列军方继续在被占领的约旦河西岸开展大规模行动，在以色列即将举行的选举之前对人员流动实施重大限制。
此次行动是为了回应周五在希伯伦发生的枪击事件，造成两名以色列士兵死亡、三人受伤，过去两天已导致数百名巴勒斯坦人流离失所。
希伯伦市政府表示，已有 2,200 多人流离失所，其中包括近 200 名 18 岁以下儿童。希伯伦市长尤瑟夫·祖海尔·贾巴里 (Yousef Zuhair Al-Jabari) 表示，自周五袭击事件以来，该市的所有出入口均保持封锁，行动的中心位于代尔巴哈 (Deir Bahha) 和该市另一个名为阿尔贾尔达 (Al-Jalda) 的地区。
“人们无法到达或进入这座城市，也无法离开它。封锁影响了生活的方方面面，”贾巴里说。
以色列军方表示，周末在 400 多个不同地点开展行动，逮捕了 40 名据称与哈马斯或巴勒斯坦伊斯兰圣战组织有关联的巴勒斯坦人。
此外，以色列军方表示，大多数持有许可证的巴勒斯坦工人将不被允许在周日和周一进入以色列定居点工作，进入以色列的过境点将保持关闭，直到周二以色列选举之后。
此次选举在很大程度上被视为对总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡在过去三年战争期间的领导和安全政策的公投。
今年，六名以色列人在约旦河西岸的袭击中丧生，该地区的暴力事件正在激增。据位于拉马拉的巴勒斯坦卫生部称，同一时期有 112 名巴勒斯坦人被杀。
周五的袭击引发了以色列的愤怒，内塔尼亚胡和他的右翼政府的三名成员周五下午在袭击现场发表声明，誓言要采取强有力的回应。
内塔尼亚胡说：“几周前，我们警告我们的敌人企图在选举前伤害我们、我们的公民和我们的士兵。” “我们将采取行动摧毁这个地方。”
内塔尼亚胡正在下周的选举中竞选连任，并已获得特朗普总统的支持，他面临着向巴勒斯坦袭击者展示强力武力的压力，以提升他在关心安全的以色列人中的形象。
约 300 万巴勒斯坦人和 54 万以色列定居者居住在以色列在 1967 年中东战争中占领的约旦河西岸。希伯伦是局势最紧张的城市之一，也是以色列军事保护下人口稠密的巴勒斯坦地区中心唯一有犹太定居者居住的地方。

title_en: Trump leans into Islamophobic rhetoric at Michigan rally
title_zh: 特朗普在密歇根集会上倾向于仇视伊斯兰教的言论
summary: The president attacked Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic Senate nominee who is locked in a dead heat against Republican Mike Rogers.
summary_zh: 总统攻击了民主党参议院候选人阿卜杜勒·赛义德，他与共和党人迈克·罗杰斯陷入了胶着状态。
body_en: Trump and Obama rally supporters in key battleground states ahead of midterms

President Donald Trump embraced Islamophobic rhetoric Sunday as he rallied in Port Huron, Michigan, in support of the state’s Republican candidates, including the GOP Senate nominee, former Rep. Mike Rogers.

Trump alleged that Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic Senate nominee who is locked in a dead heat with Rogers, is a “jihadist,” calling him a “Muslim Brotherhood member” while saying Rogers is “apple pie.”

“Anyone with that record of support for jihadists would be screened and unable to get a seat on an airplane. They certainly should not give him a seat in the United States Senate,” Trump said about El-Sayed.
Throughout his comments Sunday, Trump offered no evidence for any of the claims about El-Sayed.
“He would be the only senator that will have to go through a metal detector before he’s allowed to go into the Senate. I want him to have a metal detector,” Trump said.

Trump sought to draw a comparison between the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks and El-Sayed as he introduced speaker David Beamer, whose son, Todd Beamer, was a passenger who died on the hijacked United Flight 93.
“Twenty-five years later, Michigan needs to stand up and fight just like Todd did to stop a jihadist from walking into the Capitol,” Trump said.
Beamer went on to extend Trump’s comparison between the Senate race and 9/11.

“What has changed? Well, one thing is 9/11 was a surprise attack. What’s going on right now in our country and here in Michigan? It’s not a surprise. We can see the attack coming that culminates in this battleground state on Tuesday, November the 3rd,” Beamer said as Trump stood behind him onstage.
“What’s different this time is the enemy has not come from abroad. The enemy is right here among us, local terrorists, local citizens that want to demolish our country,” he added.
Beamer, who has been featured in Rogers’ campaign ads, compared the two men and claimed Rogers is “an American” while saying El-Sayed is not, going on to call him “anti-American.”
“Abdul has a birth certificate. The birth certificate says he’s a citizen of America. You know what? A birth certificate doesn’t make you an American,” Beamer said.
“He has blood that’s red. However, he has chosen to remove any strain of the white and blue part in his life. We cannot, cannot allow this man to invade and occupy our country,” he added.
Both Rogers and El-Sayed were born in Michigan.
El-Sayed’s campaign did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Trump’s and Beamer’s remarks.
El-Sayed went viral for a heated interaction last week with a town hall attendee who asked him to condemn the organization.
“You assume ... that because I am Muslim that somehow I would have some allegiance to something that is not our Constitution,” El-Sayed told the attendee last week.

Trump has accused El-Sayed of having ties to the Muslim Brotherhood, an international Sunni Islamist organization founded in Egypt in 1928. The Trump administration has designated certain chapters of the group in Lebanon, Jordan and Egypt as terrorist organizations. El-Sayed has repeatedly denied any ties to the group, which he has denounced.

Rogers was asked Sunday about Trump’s calling El-Sayed a “Muslim Brotherhood jihadist” and a “violent terrorist” in an interview on NBC’s “Meet the Press.” Pressed about whether he agreed with Trump’s characterizations, Rogers said the election is about “me versus Abdul,” adding, “I’ve never called him a terrorist.”
body_zh: 中期选举前，特朗普和奥巴马在关键战场州集结支持者
唐纳德·特朗普总统周日在密歇根州休伦港集会时发表了仇视伊斯兰教的言论，支持该州的共和党候选人，其中包括共和党参议院候选人、前众议员迈克·罗杰斯。
特朗普声称与罗杰斯不和的民主党参议院候选人阿卜杜勒·赛义德是一名“圣战分子”，称他为“穆斯林兄弟会成员”，同时称罗杰斯是“苹果派”。
“任何有支持圣战分子记录的人都会受到筛查，并且无法在飞机上找到座位。他们当然不应该给他在美国参议院的席位，”特朗普谈到埃尔-赛义德时说道。 “他将是唯一一位在被允许进入参议院之前必须通过金属探测器的参议员。我希望他有一个金属探测器。”
在周日的讲话中，特朗普没有提供任何证据来证明有关埃尔赛义德的任何说法。
“他将是唯一一位在被允许进入参议院之前必须通过金属探测器的参议员。我希望他有一个金属探测器，”特朗普说。
特朗普在介绍议长戴维·比默时试图将 2001 年 9 月 11 日的袭击事件与埃尔·赛义德进行比较。比默的儿子托德·比默是在被劫持的美联航 93 号航班上丧生的乘客。
特朗普说：“二十五年后，密歇根州需要像托德那样站起来并战斗，阻止圣战分子走进国会大厦。”
比默继续将特朗普的参议院竞选与 9/11 进行比较。
“发生了什么变化？嗯，有一点是，9/11 是一次突然袭击。我们国家和密歇根州现在正在发生什么？这并不奇怪。我们可以看到袭击即将到来，并在 11 月 3 日星期二在这个战场州达到顶峰，”特朗普在台上站在他身后时，比默说道。
“这次不同的是，敌人不是来自国外。敌人就在我们中间，是当地的恐怖分子，是想要摧毁我们国家的当地公民，”他补充道。
曾出现在罗杰斯竞选广告中的比默将这两个人进行了比较，并声称罗杰斯是“美国人”，而埃尔赛义德则不是，并称他为“反美国人”。
“阿卜杜勒有出生证明。出生证明上说他是美国公民。你知道吗？出生证明并不意味着你就是美国人，”比默说。
“他的血液是红色的。然而，他选择消除生命中白色和蓝色部分的任何张力。我们不能、不能允许这个人入侵和占领我们的国家，”他补充道。
罗杰斯和埃尔-赛义德都出生于密歇根州。
赛义德的竞选团队没有立即回应对特朗普和比默言论发表评论的请求。
上周，埃尔-赛义德因与一名市政厅与会者的激烈互动而走红，与会者要求他谴责该组织。
“你认为……因为我是穆斯林，所以我会以某种方式效忠一些不属于我们宪法的东西，”赛义德上周告诉与会者。
特朗普指责埃尔-赛义德与穆斯林兄弟会有联系，穆斯林兄弟会是一个 1928 年在埃及成立的国际逊尼派伊斯兰组织。特朗普政府已将该组织在黎巴嫩、约旦和埃及的某些分会指定为恐怖组织。埃尔-赛义德一再否认与该组织有任何关系，并对此予以谴责。
周日，罗杰斯在接受美国全国广播公司(NBC)“会见媒体”节目时被问及特朗普称埃尔-赛义德为“穆斯林兄弟会圣战分子”和“暴力恐怖分子”一事。当被问及他是否同意特朗普的描述时，罗杰斯表示，这次选举是关于“我与阿卜杜勒”的斗争，并补充说，“我从未称他为恐怖分子。”

title_en: Scoop: Netanyahu presses Trump for more support ahead of tight Tuesday election
title_zh: 独家新闻：内塔尼亚胡在周二紧张的选举之前向特朗普施压，要求他提供更多支持
summary: TEL AVIV, Israel — Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu — fighting for political survival in Tuesday's elections — has pleaded with President Trump in recent days to show more public support for his campaign, according to a U.S. source with knowledge and
summary_zh: 以色列特拉维夫 — 以色列总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡 — 在周二的选举中为政治生存而奋斗 — 向特鲁总统恳求
body_en: TEL AVIV, Israel — Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu — fighting for political survival in Tuesday's elections — has pleaded with President Trump in recent days to show more public support for his campaign, according to a U.S. source with knowledge and an Israeli source briefed on the matter.
Why it matters: The U.S. source said the White House sees Netanyahu's aggressive lobbying as a "sign of desperation" and an indication that the Israeli leader thinks he's trailing.
Neta Molcho, a spokesperson for Netanyahu's Likud party, denied the prime minister asked Trump to support his campaign "in recent days or before his endorsement statement."
The White House did not respond to a request for comment. Trump said in an interview with Newsmax two weeks ago that people in Israel asked him to get involved in support of Netanyahu.
Behind the scenes: The U.S. source said Netanyahu spoke with Trump twice in the last three days and asked him to double down on his Truth Social post last week endorsing him.
The source said Netanyahu even suggested language for additional statements of support.
An Israeli source briefed on Netanyahu's efforts said the Israeli prime minister proposed that Trump hold calls with Israeli reporters to express further support.
Driving the news: After weeks of hesitation, Trump endorsed Netanyahu last Sunday. He went as far as to suggest his defeat would have consequences for U.S.-Israel relations.
Trump has never worked with an Israeli prime minister other than Netanyahu, and he doesn't personally know any of the other candidates. The two have forged a close but often turbulent relationship.
State of play: Three major Israeli television networks released their final pre-election polls Friday, all showing Netanyahu's coalition falling well short of a parliamentary majority.

All three projected just 50 seats for Netanyahu's bloc in the 120-member Knesset — 17 fewer than his current coalition holds. His Likud party, which currently holds 32 seats, was projected to win just 20.

The polls gave former military chief Gadi Eisenkot's opposition bloc between 52 and 56 seats, with another 14–16 going to two Arab Israeli parties. Channel 11 also projected four seats for a reservists party unaffiliated with either bloc.
Pro-Netanyahu Channel 14 was the major outlier, projecting 60 seats for his bloc and 30 for Likud in a poll earlier this week.
Between the lines: One U.S. official described the endorsement as a win-win for Trump, regardless of the outcome.
If Netanyahu wins — or remains in power as a caretaker prime minister — Trump could claim credit for rescuing him politically and use that leverage to press for concessions.

If Netanyahu loses and his opponents form a government, Israel's new leaders would still have every incentive to cultivate good relations with Trump. His endorsement of their rival would quickly become a footnote.
Yes, but: Some of Trump's advisers see opportunity for his Middle East agenda in an Israeli government led by someone else.
body_zh: 以色列特拉维夫——据一位知情的美国消息人士和一位了解情况的以色列消息人士透露，在周二的选举中为政治生存而奋斗的以色列总理本雅明内塔尼亚胡最近几天恳求特朗普总统对他的竞选活动表现出更多的公众支持。
为什么重要：美国消息人士称，白宫将内塔尼亚胡积极的游说视为“绝望的迹象”，并表明这位以色列领导人认为他正在落后。
内塔尼亚胡领导的利库德集团发言人内塔·莫尔乔否认总理“在最近几天或在发表背书声明之前”要求特朗普支持他的竞选活动。
白宫没有回应置评请求。特朗普两周前接受Newsmax采访时表示，以色列民众要求他参与支持内塔尼亚胡。
幕后花絮：美国消息人士称，内塔尼亚胡在过去三天内与特朗普两次通话，并要求他加大上周在《真相社会》帖子上对他的支持。
消息人士称，内塔尼亚胡甚至建议使用额外的支持声明。
一位了解内塔尼亚胡努力的以色列消息人士称，以色列总理提议特朗普与以色列记者通话以表达进一步的支持。
推动新闻：经过数周的犹豫之后，特朗普于上周日支持了内塔尼亚胡。他甚至暗示他的失败将对美以关系产生影响。
除了内塔尼亚胡之外，特朗普从未与以色列总理合作过，他个人也不认识任何其他候选人。两人建立了密切但经常动荡的关系。
现状：以色列三大电视网络周五公布了最终的选举前民意调查，所有民意调查均显示内塔尼亚胡的联盟远未获得议会多数席位。
三人都预测内塔尼亚胡的集团在议会 120 名成员中仅获得 50 个席位，比他目前的联盟所拥有的席位少 17 个。他的利库德集团目前拥有 32 个席位，预计只会赢得 20 个席位。
民意调查显示，前军事首领加迪·艾森科特的反对党集团获得了 52 至 56 个席位，另外两个阿拉伯以色列政党获得了 14 比 16 的席位。 Channel 11 还为与任何一个集团都无关的预备役政党安排了四个席位。
支持内塔尼亚胡的 Channel 14 是一个主要的异常值，在本周早些时候的一项民意调查中，预计他的集团将获得 60 个席位，利库德集团将获得 30 个席位。
言外之意是：一位美国官员称，无论结果如何，对特朗普的支持都是双赢。
如果内塔尼亚胡获胜——或者作为看守总理继续掌权——特朗普可能会因在政治上拯救他而获得赞誉，并利用这一影响力迫使他让步。
如果内塔尼亚胡失败并且他的对手组建政府，以色列新领导人仍然有充分的动力与特朗普建立良好关系。他对对手的支持很快就成为一个脚注。
是的，但是：特朗普的一些顾问在由其他人领导的以色列政府中看到了他的中东议程的机会。

Trump escalates rhetoric against El-Sayed as he tries to undermine Democrat in Michigan Senate race
Politics Updated on Oct 25, 2026 8:41 PM EDT — Published on Oct 25, 2026 5:50 PM EDT

PORT HURON, Mich. (AP) — President Donald Trump intensified his anti-Muslim rhetoric against Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed on Sunday, portraying him as a threat to national security and questioning his loyalty to the United States in remarks that drew a sharp rebuke from a former top Arab American ally.

Trump called El-Sayed, a former Detroit health official, a "jihadist" who was "on the side of the terrorists" and would "have to go through a metal detector before he's allowed to go into the Senate." He also repeatedly invoked the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks, drawing a comparison between stopping El-Sayed from entering the Senate chamber and the passengers who fought back against the hijackers aboard United Flight 93.

El-Sayed, who would become the nation's first Muslim senator if elected, has called attacks on his loyalty to the country "shameful" and repeatedly denied any ties to extremist groups. The Republican president's remarks were condemned by Bishara Bahbah, a founder of Arab Americans for Trump, the group that helped lead the president's outreach to Arab American voters in 2024.
"The president's statements are out of line," he said in a phone interview. "They are crossing a red line. They are racist."

With Republicans on the defensive over inflation, soaring fuel prices and the Iran war, the president has been trying to generate turnout by claiming that El-Sayed and other Democrats are existential threats to America, instead of electoral rivals. Michigan's Senate race between El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers is among a handful of contests that could determine control of the chamber.

Trump made his remarks in Port Huron, a Canadian border city about an hour north of Detroit and near communities where he made significant gains among Arab American voters in 2024. He became the first Republican presidential candidate since 2000 to win Dearborn, a city with one of the nation's largest concentrations of Arab Americans.

Trump, who imposed a travel ban targeting several predominantly Muslim countries during his first term, has increasingly leaned into anti-Muslim rhetoric as Election Day approaches. He also attacked Democratic Rep. Ilhan Omar of Minnesota at Sunday's rally, where he declared that he had come to Michigan "to keep a jihadist Muslim Brotherhood member from becoming a United States senator."

Cole Wozniak, a spokesperson for El-Sayed, responded to Trump's comments in a statement: "While they lie and resort to desperate, bad faith attacks, Abdul remains laser focused on his plans to bring down costs and stand up to the chaos and corruption in Washington."
El-Sayed's faith, associations and past statements become campaign flashpoints

Central to Republicans' strategy against El-Sayed in the final weeks of the campaign has been an effort to link him to the Muslim Brotherhood, an Islamic movement with branches that the U.S. government has designated as terrorist organizations.

There is no evidence that El-Sayed has any affiliation with the Muslim Brotherhood. His half-sister, Eman Abdelhadi, wrote on social media in 2012 that "my family has long been MB" and described a conversation with her mother about her involvement in the Muslim Brotherhood in the early 1970s.
El-Sayed was born in the United States to Egyptian immigrant parents who divorced when he was young. He was raised by his father, not his biological mother.
Trump on Sunday also targeted El-Sayed's ties to popular streamer Hasan Piker, who appeared alongside the Democrat multiple times during the primary campaign, including at his election night event.
Piker in the past has said that "Hamas is a thousand times better" than Israel, describing some Orthodox Jews as "inbred" and that "America deserved 9/11."

El-Sayed has faced criticism for his own rhetoric. He has repeatedly refused to answer questions about whether Iran or Israel poses a bigger threat to the country. Earlier this year, he said "hurt people hurt people" after an attack on a synagogue in the Detroit area. The attacker had lost four relatives in an Israeli airstrike on Lebanon the week earlier. El-Sayed later apologized, saying he was not trying to justify what happened.
